english: Three of ten chairs placed in a row are chosen at random. Let $p$ be the probability that no two of the chosen chairs are adjacent, and let $q$ be the probability that the three chosen chairs are consecutive. Then the value of $q-p$ is ______.
hindi: एक पंक्ति में रखी दस कुर्सियों में से तीन कुर्सियाँ यादृच्छया चुनी जाती हैं। माना कि $p$ चुनी गई कुर्सियों में से किन्हीं दो के आसन्न न होने की प्रायिकता है, तथा $q$ तीनों चुनी गई कुर्सियों के क्रमागत होने की प्रायिकता है। तब $q-p$ का मान ______ है।
solution: No two adjacent: 7 unchosen chairs make 8 gaps; choose 3 gaps: $\binom{8}{3}=56$
solution_full: No two chosen chairs adjacent: place the 7 unchosen chairs in a row; they form 8 gaps (including both ends), and choosing 3 different gaps for the chosen chairs gives exactly the choices with no two adjacent. Number: $\binom{8}{3}=56$, so $p=\dfrac{56}{120}$.
Three consecutive chairs: the block can start at chair $1,2,\ldots,8$, so $8$ choices and $q=\dfrac{8}{120}$.
originality_note: New: the two extreme spacing events for a random 3-subset of a row (all separated, all together) compared through their probabilities (way 5). Closest known: 'number of ways of choosing r of n chairs with no two adjacent: C(n-r+1, r)'. Different because: the answer is a signed comparison with the opposite extreme.
blueprint_concepts: Selecting r objects from n in a row with no two consecutive

concept_use.Selecting r objects from n in a row with: The 'no two adjacent' count is C(10-3+1, 3) = C(8,3) = 56 by the gap argument; the consecutive count 8 is the opposite extreme.
